subject: Generating SE for basic frequency stats

messages.author: 7f8074a18bec5412
messages.subject: Generating SE for basic frequency stats
parts:
Hi,

I'm just trying to report some basic frequency stats for 5 populations (8 loci). Through various functions, I've been able to get mean Ho or He for each locus (over all 5 pops) or mean Ho or He for each pop (over all 8 loci). How can I get the standard error for each of these values?

Also, is it possible to generate a poppr table that displays values for each locus for each population (locus*pop)?

Thanks,
Leah

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: Generating SE for basic frequency stats
parts:
I realize that I sent this to Leah, but not to the group (sorry for the double posting, Leah)

Assuming that you have the 40 values of Ho/He (8 X 5) necessary to calculate the means, you can calculate standard error from the mean by defining the function se <- function(x) sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)) and using that on each column/row of the 8x5 matrix.

Here's an example of extracting the Hexp mean and se for the first five populations of the nancycats data set:

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("poppr"))
data(nancycats)
n5 <- seppop(nancycats, drop = FALSE)[1:5]
Ho <- function(x) summary(x)$Hobs
He <- function(x) locus_table(x, information = FALSE)[seq(nLoc(x)), "Hexp", drop = TRUE]
se <- function(x) sd(x)/length(x)
He_overall<- sapply(n5, FUN = He)
He_overall
#>             P01       P02       P03       P04       P05
#> fca8  0.6416667 0.7875264 0.7753623 0.8115942 0.8091954
#> fca23 0.7210526 0.6300211 0.8768116 0.7864734 0.6850575
#> fca43 0.7789474 0.7008457 0.7500000 0.7207729 0.8160920
#> fca45 0.6789474 0.7505285 0.6884058 0.7159420 0.7885057
#> fca77 0.7842105 0.8636364 0.7898551 0.8096618 0.7678161
#> fca78 0.5263158 0.6617336 0.6739130 0.7903382 0.3931034
#> fca90 0.7263158 0.6987315 0.7862319 0.8289855 0.6620690
#> fca96 0.6263158 0.5465116 0.6992754 0.7285024 0.6482759
#> fca37 0.3578947 0.6712474 0.4311594 0.5555556 0.1931034
He_mean_pop <- colMeans(He_overall)
He_se_pop <- apply(He_overall, MARGIN = 2, FUN = se)
He_by_pop <- data.frame(He = He_mean_pop, se = He_se_pop)
He_by_pop
#>            He         se
#> P01 0.6490741 0.01509212
#> P02 0.7011980 0.01022336
#> P03 0.7190016 0.01387738
#> P04 0.7497585 0.00936519
#> P05 0.6403576 0.02361227


Note that if you want to calculate that by locus instead, you would use rowMeans and MARGIN = 1.

Hope that helps,
Zhian
